_comment: DO NOT GUESS. Backup-care coverage (childcare, pet-sitting, elder care, or any other dependent coverage) is set ONLY by the user, per hub — never inferred by a model. An earlier version INVENTED per-city likelihoods (e.g. 'San Diego: likely', 'Phoenix: likely') and let them rank studies. That was wrong and is removed. This file ships as ANONYMIZED EXAMPLE data only — generic city + coverage note, never a real friend's name or identifying detail. Default every hub to no free coverage; the user decides study-by-study whether has_dependents_needing_care even applies to them (lib/types.ts's Assumptions.has_dependents_needing_care), and free coverage below is only ever used when they've turned that on.
rule: Never assign backup-care coverage from a model. Only the user sets it (backup_care_available, below, is user-stated example data, not a guess). Ranking MUST NOT depend on guessed coverage — rank on pay, nights, drive-vs-fly, payout timing, eligibility. home_base is any city the visitor enters (lib/types.ts's HomeBase) — 'austin'/'omaha' are not special-cased anywhere; drivable-vs-fly is computed from the coordinates below via lib/scoring.ts's haversine distance check, not a hardcoded per-city hub list.

SLC.note: Example: user has friends there who could provide backup-care coverage (childcare or otherwise).

SA.note: Example: hub is a short drive from an example home base and the user has contacts there who offered to help for a weekend stay. Nothing beyond that is confirmed.
